newsitem.title: UK: Britain's wet June helps reservoir supplies-report.
newsitem.headline: Britain's wet June helps reservoir supplies-report.

text.p: Britain's water supplies from groundwater are still low despite heavy rainfall in June after a two-year drought, the Water Services Association (WSA) said on Wednesday.
Groundwater levels in all areas except Northumbrian, northern England, are low, the WSA said in a statement, despite record-breaking June rainfall which also helped to dampen consumption.
Reservoirs, meanwhile, were helped by the rain and most are now at or above normal levels for the time of year, with the exception of Anglian, in eastern England, Southern and South West regions.
There are currently no bans in force on using hosepipes in any area, but Southern continues a long-standing restriction on the use of sprinklers in parts of Sussex.
Water companies came under severe criticism for their handling of the drought, the worst for 200 years, as many struggled to maintain supplies.

The new Labour government called a crisis summit two weeks after it came to power on May 1 and forced companies to respond to a 10-point plan to improve the industry, which included mandatory targets for cutting leaks and offering free repairs to pipes of customers.
